summary.headline: The Select Board voted against supporting a $217,318 trail bridge expansion while endorsing seven other Special Town Meeting warrant articles.
summary.summary: Meeting in a joint session with the Advisory Committee, the Southborough Select Board reviewed proposed warrant articles for the upcoming Special Town Meeting, including zoning for two-family dwellings and CPA requests. The board ultimately voted 1-4 against supporting additional CPA funding for a pedestrian bridge on the Peninsula Trail, while unanimously supporting a $1.087 million golf course irrigation system project. The Select Board also acted as Water Commissioners to grant partial abatement on a high water bill, approved municipal paving and fuel contracts, and debated updates to municipal procurement and budget policies.

topics.title: Zoning amendment for two-family dwellings
topics.summary: Zoning Board of Appeals representative Doris Cahill presented a proposed warrant article to eliminate the mandatory two-year waiting period to convert a single-family house into a two-family dwelling or build new two-family housing. The change aims to clarify zoning definitions, differentiate two-family homes from accessory dwelling units, and encourage affordable housing options. Members discussed density concerns, lot requirements, and potential floor amendments at Town Meeting.
key_details: Eliminates the two-year waiting period to convert a single-family dwelling to a two-family home.
Allows new construction of two-family homes by special permit.
Clarifies definitions to differentiate two-family dwellings from accessory dwelling units.
Planning Board suggested minor wording revisions prior to Town Meeting.
Select Board voted 4-1 later in the meeting to recommend the article.
topics.outcome: Select Board voted 4-1 to recommend approval at Special Town Meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: Changes would make it easier to construct or convert two-family homes across residential zones in town, impacting neighborhood density and housing availability.

topics.title: CPA request for Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge
topics.summary: The Trails Committee and Community Preservation Committee presented an article requesting $217,318 in additional CPA funds for a 65-foot prefabricated pedestrian bridge along the Peninsula Trail on the Framingham border. The initial 2024 appropriation of $211,232 was insufficient after bids came in significantly higher than expected, leading to a redesigned, smaller project scope with a total estimated cost of $428,550. Several Advisory Committee and Select Board members criticized the cost and questioned whether municipal recreation funds should take priority over operating budget strains.
key_details: Requested an additional $217,318 in CPA funding, bringing total project cost to $428,550.
Covers a 65-foot prefabricated fiberglass-reinforced polymer bridge along Route 30.
Original scope included a boardwalk and paving, but those were removed or funded separately.
Trails Committee plans to apply for a $100,000 MassTrails grant in 2027 to partially reimburse funds.
Advisory Committee member Al Hamilton called the project a bridge to nowhere.
topics.outcome: Select Board voted 1-4 against supporting the warrant article.
topics.why_it_matters: The project would spend over $400,000 in CPA funds to connect pedestrian trail segments, but failed to win Select Board support due to cost concerns.

topics.title: CPA request for golf course irrigation system
topics.summary: Golf Committee Chair Tony Schunner and DPW Director Bill Cundiff requested supplementary funding to replace the failing irrigation system at the municipal golf course, bringing total project funding to $1,087,000. An initial $500,000 approval proved inadequate when bids arrived between $800,000 and $850,000, requiring engineering redesigns, a new pump station, and directional boring. The request includes $100,000 from the Golf Course Revolving Fund, with the remaining balance funded by the Community Preservation Act.
key_details: Total revised project budget is $1,087,000, up from the original $500,000 appropriation.
Golf Course Revolving Fund will contribute $100,000 toward the total cost.
Redesign includes horizontal boring under streams and an added booster pump station.
Construction is estimated to take six weeks during the playing season using cordoned work areas.
Select Board voted 5-0 later in the meeting to recommend the article with minor corrections.
topics.outcome: Select Board voted 5-0 to recommend approval at Special Town Meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: The town is committing over $1 million to maintain the municipal golf course asset, addressing infrastructure needed to keep the course operational and commercially viable.

topics.title: Appointments to Tri-Centennial Committee
topics.summary: The Select Board interviewed and appointed two residents, Amy Dennis and Terry Picard, to open seats on the Tri-Centennial Committee to help organize upcoming town 300th anniversary events. The appointments are for terms expiring June 30, 2027, subject to committee confirmation.
key_details: Candidates bring background experience in corporate operations, risk management, and local volunteering.
Appointments run through June 30, 2027.
Town 300th anniversary celebration preparations are accelerating with under four months until the anniversary year.

topics.title: Cemetery Expansion Committee membership charge reduction
topics.summary: The Select Board updated the charge of the ad hoc Cemetery Expansion Committee to reduce its membership from five to three members to help achieve consistent meeting quorums.
key_details: Membership reduced from 5 to 3 members.
Change is effective immediately.

topics.title: Town administrative and regional transit updates
topics.summary: The chair reported the appointment of Amy Peery as Interim Town Clerk effective October 1, ahead of Jim Hegarty's upcoming retirement. Select Board member Sam Stivers reported that the MetroWest Regional Transit Authority launched two new bus routes connecting the commuter rail station to the Solomon Pond Mall area and Route 9 businesses. Town Administrator Mark Purple announced that a consultant studying municipal government structure will present initial findings to the board on October 6.
key_details: Amy Peery appointed Interim Town Clerk starting September 23 with full appointment effective October 1 through May 11, 2027.
MWRTA introduced Route 302 and Route 309 connecting local transit hubs fare-free.
Community Software Solutions government structure survey due September 22; consultant presentation set for October 6, 2026.
The annual 9/11 anniversary remembrance ceremony was held the previous Friday.
topics.outcome: Informational updates only; no formal vote taken.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board approved consent agenda items B, E, G, H, and J, and approved the minutes of the September 2 and September 4 meetings as amended.
key_details: Approved consent agenda items unanimously.
Approved meeting minutes of September 2 and September 4 with minor spelling corrections.

topics.title: Contracts for FY27 road paving, sidewalks, and fuel oil
topics.summary: DPW Director Bill Cundiff presented contract awards for fiscal year 2027 road paving, sidewalk maintenance, and municipal heating oil. Paving bids came in roughly $400,000 below engineering estimates, covering six roads including sections of Cordaville Road and Cranberry Road. The board also awarded the municipal #2 fuel oil contract.
key_details: Paving covers six roads, including interim maintenance on Cordaville and Cranberry roads ahead of long-term state TIP projects.
Bid pricing came in well below engineering estimates.
Fuel oil contract for fiscal year 2027 awarded to Bellco Energy at $2.99 per gallon.
topics.outcome: Select Board approved both contract awards unanimously, 5-0.
topics.why_it_matters: Favorable paving bids allow the DPW to complete planned road and sidewalk improvements below budget across several major corridors.

topics.title: Water bill appeal: 104 Boston Road
topics.summary: Acting as the Water Commissioners, the Select Board considered an appeal by Carolyn Golbankian regarding a $2,872.03 water bill resulting from an underground pipe leak during February and March. The normal quarterly bill is approximately $280, and the town wholesale water cost from the MWRA for the excess volume was roughly $639. The board agreed to grant a partial abatement, setting the final bill amount at $1,100.
key_details: One member recused due to a business relationship with the property owner.
Pipe leak resulted in an uncharacteristically high bill of $2,872.03.
Town out-of-pocket wholesale water cost was approximately $639.
DPW noted that commercial insurance for private service lines is available for about $5 per month.
topics.outcome: Select Board approved reducing the bill to $1,100 on a 4-0-1 vote (one member recused).

topics.title: Municipal financial and procurement policies
topics.summary: The Select Board reviewed several municipal financial policies, approving updates to the purchasing policy while shelving the state DOR reserve policy recommendations because the town does not hold the recommended reserve levels. The board engaged in a detailed discussion about a proposed budget policy defining the respective roles of the Select Board, Town Administrator, and Advisory Committee in budget development and warrant preparation, deciding to consult Town Counsel and the Department of Revenue.
key_details: DOR reserve policy shelved to prevent bond rating downgrades for having policies the town cannot meet.
Purchasing policy approved with clerical updates.
Conflict of interest policy for bid evaluations tabled pending Town Counsel review.
Budget development policy tabled to seek clarification from state officials on statutory versus advisory committee roles.
topics.outcome: Purchasing policy approved 5-0; other policies tabled or shelved.

topics.title: Warrant article positions for Special Town Meeting
topics.summary: The Select Board voted on formal positions for eight Special Town Meeting warrant articles. The board endorsed seven articles including the town clerk vacancy, two-family zoning amendments, golf course irrigation, stormwater exploration, rescinding unissued debt, water main extensions, and raising the personal property tax exemption, but opposed the Peninsula Trail bridge.
key_details: Article 1 (Town Clerk vacancy): Supported 5-0.
Article 2 (Two-family dwellings zoning): Supported 4-1.
Article 3 (Golf course irrigation CPA): Supported 5-0 with clerical amendments.
Article 4 (Peninsula Trail bridge CPA): Support failed 1-4.
Article 5 (Stormwater exploration): Supported 4-1.
Article 6 (Rescind authorized unissued debt): Supported 5-0.
topics.outcome: Select Board finalized positions for the Special Town Meeting warrant.
topics.why_it_matters: Select Board recommendations will be printed in the warrant booklet guiding voters at the upcoming Special Town Meeting.

public_comment.summary: A resident spoke in favor of granting full water bill relief to Golbankian Farms, noting its long history in town since 1920, and urged the town to expedite the installation of smart water meters to help prevent surprise leak bills.
